subproblem.title: C¹ cut-off of f near K to a compact perturbation of the identity supported in O
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, O ⊆ ℝ^P open, K ⊆ O compact, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ on O (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O; f is arbitrary off O). Then there exist a map φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ on all of ℝ^P (ContDiff ℝ 1 φ), an open set V ⊆ ℝ^P with K ⊆ V, and a compact set K' with K' ⊆ O, such that φ(x) = f(x) and Dφ(x) = Df(x) for every x ∈ V (Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x), and φ(x) = x for every x ∉ K'.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (O K : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen O → IsCompact K → K ⊆ O → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O → ∃ (φ : Euclid P → Euclid P) (V K' : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen V ∧ K ⊆ V ∧ IsCompact K' ∧ K' ⊆ O ∧ ContDiff ℝ 1 φ ∧ (∀ x ∈ V, φ x = f x ∧ fderiv ℝ φ x = fderiv ℝ f x) ∧ ∀ x, x ∉ K' → φ x = x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 (Cutoffs) of the parent proof, specialized. The parent cuts f off to g = χ₁·f with g = f near K. Here the cut-off is taken relative to the identity, φ = χ·f + (1 − χ)·id, so that in addition φ = id off a compact subset of O. The parent's conclusion "g(x) = f(x) and Dg(x) = Df(x) on a neighbourhood of K" is kept.
Notation: E := ℝ^P (Euclid P, a finite-dimensional and hence proper real normed space); thickening r K := {z : infEdist(z, K) < r}; cthickening r K := {z : infEdist(z, K) ≤ r}; Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x.
1. Margin. K is compact, O is open and K ⊆ O, so there is δ > 0 with cthickening δ K ⊆ O (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Put s := thickening δ K (open, isOpen_thickening), t := cthickening (δ/2) K (closed, isClosed_cthickening) and V := thickening (δ/2) K (open, isOpen_thickening). Then K ⊆ V (self_subset_thickening, since δ/2 > 0), V ⊆ t (thickening_subset_cthickening), and t ⊆ s (cthickening_subset_thickening', since 0 < δ and δ/2 < δ). If K = ∅, all these sets are empty and the steps below go through unchanged.
2. Smooth cutoff. Apply the smooth Urysohn lemma in the finite-dimensional real space E (Mathlib exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff, with smoothness order ⊤ : ℕ∞) to the open set s and the closed set t ⊆ s. It gives χ : E → ℝ, C^∞, with values in [0, 1], support χ = s, and χ(x) = 1 ⟺ x ∈ t. In particular χ is C¹ (ContDiff.of_le), and χ = 1 on V ⊆ t.
3. The compact set K'. Let K' := tsupport χ = closure (support χ) = closure s. Then K' ⊆ cthickening δ K (closure_thickening_subset_cthickening) ⊆ O by step 1. K' is closed (isClosed_tsupport) and lies in the compact set cthickening δ K (IsCompact.cthickening, E proper), so K' is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset).
4. Definition. For x ∈ E put φ(x) := χ(x)·f(x) + (1 − χ(x))·x. No regularity of f off O is used.
5. φ = id off K'. If x ∉ K' = tsupport χ, then χ(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), so φ(x) = 0·f(x) + 1·x = x.
6. φ = f near K. Let x ∈ V. Since V is open, it is a neighbourhood of x. Every y ∈ V lies in t, so χ(y) = 1 and φ(y) = 1·f(y) + 0·y = f(y). Thus φ and f agree on a neighbourhood of x (φ =ᶠ[𝓝 x] f). This gives φ(x) = f(x) (Filter.EventuallyEq.eq_of_nhds) and Dφ(x) = Df(x) (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq: the Fréchet derivative at x depends only on the germ at x).
7. φ is C¹ on E. By contDiff_iff_contDiffAt it suffices to show ContDiffAt ℝ 1 φ x for every x ∈ E.
 (a) x ∈ O. O is open, so O ∈ 𝓝 x and f is C¹ at x (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt). χ is C¹ at x by step 2, and the constant 1 and the identity are C¹. The product of a real C¹ function with a vector-valued C¹ map is C¹ at x, and so are sums and differences of C¹ maps (ContDiffAt.smul, ContDiffAt.add, ContDiffAt.sub). Hence φ = χ·f + (1 − χ)·id is C¹ at x.
 (b) x ∉ O. Then x ∉ K', because K' ⊆ O (step 3). The complement of the closed set K' is an open neighbourhood of x on which φ = id (step 5). So φ =ᶠ[𝓝 x] id, and φ is C¹ at x (ContDiffAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq with contDiffAt_id).
8. Conclusion. The triple (φ, V, K') has all required properties:
 - V is open and K ⊆ V (step 1);
 - K' is compact and K' ⊆ O (step 3);
 - φ is C¹ on E (step 7);
 - φ(x) = f(x) and Dφ(x) = Df(x) for every x ∈ V (step 6);
 - φ(x) = x for every x ∉ K' (step 5). ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose δ > 0 with cthickening δ K ⊆ O; V := thickening (δ/2) K is an open neighbourhood of K, contained in t := cthickening (δ/2) K ⊆ s := thickening δ K.
Smooth Urysohn (exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff): χ ∈ C^∞(E, [0,1]) with support χ = s and χ = 1 exactly on t; K' := tsupport χ ⊆ cthickening δ K ⊆ O is compact.
φ := χ·f + (1 − χ)·id equals id off K' and equals f on the open set V, hence φ = f and Dφ = Df on V (EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq).
φ is C¹ at points of O (C¹ combination of χ, f, id) and at points off O (φ = id near them, as K' ⊆ O), hence ContDiff ℝ 1 φ.

audit.reason: The standalone one-line type matches every hypothesis and conclusion in the prose. The proof supplies the compact margin, smooth cutoff, compact support containment, identity outside that support, and global C¹ regularity even though f is arbitrary outside O. Equality on the open neighbourhood V gives equality of Fréchet derivatives by locality. Empty K and dimension zero cause no gap. The proof is complete and non-circular, and the bare declaration name is unreserved. Applying it on O ∩ U supplies precisely the compact perturbation required by perturbed_boundary.
